source_evidence: your brokerage firm can require you to deposit cash or securities to your account immediately. It can also sell any of the securities in your account to cover any shortfall, without informing you in advance.
answer: In a margin account, securities in your portfolio serve as collateral for money borrowed from the brokerage firm. If their value declines, the firm may issue a margin call by requiring you to add cash or securities to cover a shortfall. If the shortfall is not covered, the firm may sell securities in your account, and it may do so without advance notice. The firm chooses which securities to sell, and it may sell them before the end of any period it said you had to cover the shortfall.
